explanation: The labeled superior/inferior vena cava, aorta, pulmonary artery and veins, atria, and ventricles identify this as a dissection of the heart, demonstrating the four-chamber cardiac anatomy.
New endothelial-lined lumina forming through an organized thrombus create channels that partially restore blood flow through the previously occluded vessel.
The acid-fast (Ziehl-Neelsen) stain highlights Mycobacterium tuberculosis because its mycolic-acid-rich waxy cell wall retains carbolfuchsin even after acid-alcohol washing.
Silver stains reveal the corkscrew-shaped spirochete Treponema pallidum, the causative agent of syphilis.

The frothy casts and silver-positive cyst walls identify Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, a defining opportunistic infection of AIDS. It characteristically produces bilateral interstitial infiltrates with diffuse ground-glass opacities on CT.

Kaposi sarcoma is composed of proliferating spindled endothelial cells and is associated with HHV-8 (also called KSHV). It is a secondary neoplasm of AIDS, presenting as cutaneous, mucosal, or visceral violaceous lesions.

Primary effusion lymphoma is an aggressive B-cell lymphoma of body-cavity effusions associated with HHV-8 (often with EBV co-infection). Like other AIDS lymphomas it arises from viral-induced transformation in the setting of immunosuppression.

The diagram shows the HLA (MHC) gene complex at 6p21. These genes encode cell-surface MHC molecules that present peptide antigens, allowing the immune system to distinguish self from non-self, which is the basis of transplant matching and rejection.
Hepatitis C rarely causes symptomatic acute infection but frequently becomes chronic, marked by portal lymphocytic/lymphoplasmacytic inflammation that can progress to cirrhosis.
The trichrome stain colors collagen blue, highlighting the delicate bridging fibrosis that develops later in the course of chronic hepatitis C.
Homer Wright rosettes (radial cells around a fibrillar center) and Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes (cells around a true lumen) are both characteristic histologic features of retinoblastoma.

brick: Introduction to Pathology, Cell Injury, and Adaptation
explanation: The arrows point to mitotic figures (condensed dividing chromosomes staining dark purple). Abundant mitoses are a morphologic marker of rapid cellular proliferation, seen here in a medulloblastoma.

brick: Introduction to Pathology, Cell Injury, and Adaptation
explanation: Depleted ATP impairs Na+/K+ pumps, causing water influx and cellular swelling with pale, eosinophilic cytoplasm. This is a hallmark of reversible injury and resolves if the stimulus is removed.

The morphology (small blue cells, scant cytoplasm, nuclear molding, dispersed chromatin) is that of small cell lung carcinoma, a poorly differentiated neuroendocrine tumor derived from Kulchitsky cells. This origin explains its capacity for ectopic hormone production (ACTH, ADH) and neurologic paraneoplastic syndromes.
The bilobed, owl-eye Reed-Sternberg cell with prominent eosinophilic nucleoli is the pathognomonic histologic finding of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, roughly half of which are EBV-associated.
The pale tingible body macrophages scattered among the dark neoplastic B-cells create the 'starry sky' appearance characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.
The EBV-associated non-keratinizing (undifferentiated) subtype of nasopharyngeal carcinoma shows undifferentiated epithelial cells with a dense lymphocytic infiltrate.
A multi-lobulated, flower-shaped nucleus is seen in the acute phase of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma associated with HTLV-1 infection.
H. pylori induces chronic gastritis characterized by a mucosal infiltrate of lymphocytes and plasma cells, the first step in the cascade toward adenocarcinoma.
Intestinal metaplasia (goblet and Paneth cells replacing gastric epithelium) is a premalignant step in the H. pylori-driven progression toward gastric adenocarcinoma.
High-grade dysplasia becomes invasive gastric adenocarcinoma when the neoplastic cells invade through the basement membrane into surrounding tissues.
Extranodal marginal zone (MALT) lymphoma of the stomach is associated with H. pylori and shows an increased population of small neoplastic B-cells; many cases regress after eradication.

Apoptotic cells shrink, become densely eosinophilic, and show condensed nuclei; because apoptosis is controlled and cells are cleared by phagocytes, there is little or no inflammation. Necrosis, by contrast, spills cell contents and provokes a prominent inflammatory response.
In H&E staining, eosin stains cytoplasmic and extracellular components pink while hematoxylin stains nuclei blue-purple.

A small cell dominated by a round nucleus with scant cytoplasm is a lymphocyte. Neutrophils have multilobed nuclei, eosinophils have bilobed nuclei with red granules, monocytes are larger with reniform nuclei, and basophils contain dark blue granules.

The layer shown between epithelium and interstitium is the basement membrane, a specialized extracellular matrix rich in type IV collagen and laminin that provides an anchoring, supporting surface for the growth of epithelial, endothelial, and smooth muscle cells.
